requirements.statement: Each party section's hint reads: Place of origin 'The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'; Consignor 'This is the sender of the consignment.'; Consignee 'This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'; Importer 'This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'; Place of destination 'This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.', on the live-animals set's roles and addresses page for every commodity. The germinal-products set's copy of the page keeps the same hints.

Its internal id, route and address-book role stay as they are.

requirements.statement: An empty Place of destination row offers the link 'Add a place of destination' to the place of destination picker.

requirements.statement: Once a party has an address, its add link is replaced by a 'Change' link to that party's picker; using it and picking a different address replaces the copy on the notification.

requirements.statement: Where the CPH section shows, it is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number' with the hint 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', and once a number is entered it shows the number with a 'Change' link to the CPH number page.

requirements.statement: On the live-animals set's roles and addresses page, the CPH number section shows for every consignment except one whose commodity codes are only horses (0101) or other animals needing a permanent address (01061900). The germinal-products set's page, which shows no CPH number section at all, is this requirement's germinal half, a requirement of its own.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists which commodity codes leave the CPH number out. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 splits this requirement per set and takes the germinal lines out of the live-animals catalogue, so the live-animals set only ever meets the live codes, and it already exempts exactly 0101 and 01061900.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH row is the default and only commodity codes 0101 and 01061900 are exempt (trace-animals-fit-p14-027, repo-frontend-p9-179, repo-frontend-p9-178). The germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 are still asked today only because the live-animals catalogue holds the 12 germinal lines; taking them out (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026) is the commodity catalogue's work, not this page's.

requirements.statement: For commodity code 01061900, when at least one selected species needs a permanent address, the roles and addresses page shows a 'Permanent address' section with the hint 'A permanent address is where an animal:' and the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address'; no other consignment shows it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the permanent address among the consignment's addresses for pets; the real page shows no such section today.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a cat consignment's roles and addresses page shows only the five party rows (trace-animals-fit-p14-026). Where the link leads, and the permanent address pages themselves, belong to the cph-permanent-and-contact area.

requirements.statement: When a place of origin has been chosen and the consignor is still empty, the Consignor row offers a 'Same as place of origin' button, styled as a link, beside its 'Add a consignor' link.
requirements.why: The consignor is often the farm of origin; Design Release 2.1 lets the trader reuse it in one press. DR1 asked for the same shortcut.
requirements.deltaNote: Today choosing one party never offers to fill another (trace-animals-fit-p14-073).

requirements.statement: When a consignee has been chosen and the importer is still empty, the Importer row offers a 'Same as consignee' button, styled as a link, beside its 'Add an importer' link.
requirements.why: The importer hint already says it is usually the same as the consignee, yet today the trader has to pick it again; Design Release 2.1 and DR1 both give a shortcut.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Importer row still reads 'Not added yet' with only an add link after a consignee is chosen (trace-animals-fit-p14-073).

requirements.statement: When a consignee has been chosen and the place of destination is still empty, the Place of destination row offers a 'Same as consignee' button, styled as a link, beside its 'Add a place of destination' link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader reuse the consignee as the place of destination in one press.
requirements.deltaNote: Today no row offers to copy another (trace-animals-fit-p14-073).

requirements.statement: A same-as button shows only while its source party has an address and its target party has none; only place of origin copies to consignor, and only consignee copies to importer and place of destination.
requirements.why: The shortcut is offered only where it can help, and Design Release 2.1 has no other pairings.

requirements.statement: Pressing a same-as button submits the roles and addresses page's own form, saves on the notification a copy of the source party's record (name, address lines, country and contact details) as the target party, and reloads the page with no success banner, showing the copied address with a 'Change' link and no same-as button. The copy is independent: changing the source party later does not change it, and it is made even when the address is not one the target's picker would offer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fills the row in place with no picker; the real service must persist the copy on the notification like any other pick, and the hub's rows have to sit inside its form for the button to submit it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page's form already posts with a crumb and concurrency token (trace-animals-fit-p14-019) and a pick stores a copy of the record (repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086), but the summary list sits outside the form (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-023).

requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on the roles and addresses page never shows an error for empty sections; completeness shows only in the task status.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page both let the trader move on with sections still empty.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-027 shows the page's submit redirects without checking any answer today.

requirements.statement: On a new notification's opening run through the journey, 'Save and continue' on the roles and addresses page goes on to the contact address for this consignment page (not the CPH number page), or to the overview when every overview section is already complete. Opened from its overview task, the page returns to the overview on 'Save and continue' (req-1615); under check-your-answers change context it still returns to check your answers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 takes the trader on to the next step of the journey, the contact address, rather than to the CPH number, which it reaches only from the page's own CPH row. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 confirms that a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview and removes the criterion that ran Roles and addresses on to the CPH number page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page's submit follows the live flow (repo-frontend-p9-026): the opening run goes on to the CPH number page and then the overview (repo-tests-p1-086), and once the overview has been shown it lands on the overview (trace-animals-fit-p14-075). The opening run's next step becomes the contact address page; the overview-opened return is req-1615's change, which this page shares.

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page ends with a 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button that saves and goes to the overview, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the overview.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real page give the same three controls on this page, which the overview links to.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p14-018 shows the same three controls today.

requirements.statement: The 'Roles and addresses' task is complete only when every section shown for the consignment is complete: each party has an address, and the CPH number or permanent address is given where that section shows.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts every section the page shows towards the task, so a cattle notification is not complete without its CPH number.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the task is Complete once the five parties are picked and the page submitted (repo-frontend-p9-028, repo-frontend-p9-004); no today source shows the CPH row counting towards it (trace-animals-fit-p14-081), and the permanent address is not on this page.

requirements.statement: The overview's '5. Consignment parties' section holds the task 'Roles and addresses', with the hint 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination', linking to the roles and addresses page.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real overview already agree on the task's name and hint.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p14-001 and trace-animals-fit-p14-002 show the same task and hint today.

requirements.statement: Each party picker has the page title '<party> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the caption 'Consignment parties' directly above an h1 naming the party, and that party's hint from the roles and addresses page as its intro.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real pickers already agree on this, apart from the consignor's name.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p14-028 to -034 show the same title, caption, heading and intro today.

requirements.statement: Each party picker's Back link goes to the roles and addresses page, keeping any check-your-answers change context.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-050 and trace-e2e-p9-046 show Back going to the roles and addresses page today.

requirements.statement: Each of the five party pickers (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination) offers 'Add a new address' for its role as a secondary button beside its heading, not as a plain link under the intro; it is still left out in stub mode, where there is no address service to add to.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 presents adding an address as a button beside the heading. Where the button leads is the party-address-add-and-edit area's.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Add a new address' is a plain link in a paragraph under the intro (trace-e2e-p9-011, repo-frontend-p9-051), not offered in stub mode (repo-frontend-p9-052).

requirements.statement: The consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination pickers each have a search box labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country'.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real pickers already agree on this wording.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-053 and trace-animals-fit-p14-037 show the same label and hint today.

requirements.statement: The picker's 'Search' label is styled as a medium heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the search label medium heading weight.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is small (govuk-label--s; trace-animals-fit-p14-037).

requirements.statement: The picker's search is run by a search icon button beside the box, with the accessible name 'Search', in place of the secondary 'Search' text button; the icon button submits the picker form, so search still works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses an icon button; DR1 judged that the server-side search must stay as the no-JavaScript fallback, which a non-submitting icon button would lose.
requirements.deltaNote: Today search runs from a secondary 'Search' text button that posts the form with action=search (repo-frontend-p9-054, trace-e2e-p9-018).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, typing in a picker's search box hides the rows whose name, address lines or country do not contain the text (ignoring case) and updates the results count, with no page reload.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the list as the trader types; DR1 judged a live filter layered on the server search to be the part worth porting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker carries no client-side JavaScript (repo-frontend-p9-070, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-051); search is a server round trip only.

requirements.statement: Submitting the picker's search, or opening it with a search in the address, narrows the list on the server to matching addresses and keeps the text in the box; an empty search shows the whole list again.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the existing server-side search must stay as the fallback for traders without JavaScript, and the prototype also filters on the server when given a search.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-055 and trace-e2e-p9-036 to -040 show server-side search keeping its text, and an empty search restoring the list, today.

requirements.statement: Each party picker lists every address it offers on one page, with no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows every address for the role in one table, and DR1 judged one page with no pagination the portable half of its picker; it lands with role filtering, so the list is the role's addresses rather than the whole book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker shows five addresses a page, cut from 25-record API pages, with GOV.UK pagination (repo-frontend-p9-065 to -072, trace-e2e-p9-032 to -035); the whole book can already be read unpaginated, as the contact picker does (repo-frontend-p9-167).

requirements.statement: The picker no longer shows a 'Selected address: <name>' inset: the chosen address is always on screen as its checked row.
requirements.why: The inset exists only because the chosen row could be on another page; with one page it goes, as in Design Release 2.1 and as DR1 judged.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker restates the choice in a 'Selected address:' inset and carries it across pages in a hidden 'selected' field (repo-frontend-p9-057, repo-frontend-p9-076, trace-e2e-p9-047, trace-e2e-p9-048).

requirements.statement: Under the search, each picker shows the heading 'Select an address' above the results count.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list of addresses; DR1 asked for the same heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the results table has no heading above it; its caption carries the count (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p7-016, trace-animals-fit-p14-039).

requirements.statement: The picker's results count reads 'Showing <visible> out of <total> results', in English and Welsh, and changes as the list is filtered.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the count this way; DR1 asked for the same rewording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the table caption reads 'Showing <shown> of <total> addresses' (repo-frontend-p9-058, trace-e2e-p9-027), Welsh 'Yn dangos <shown> o <total> cyfeiriad' (repo-frontend-p9-089-m1), and says 'addresses' even for one (trace-e2e-p9-028).

requirements.statement: The picker's address table sits inside one fieldset whose legend 'Select an address' is visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups the address radios under one legend, so assistive technology announces them as one choice.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each row's radio sits in its own form group, with no fieldset or legend for the whole choice (trace-e2e-p9-022).

requirements.statement: The picker lists addresses in a table with a radio column (header 'Select', visually hidden), Name, Address and Country columns, and a last column for the row's action (header visually hidden); each row's radio has the visually hidden label 'Select <name>'.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real picker already agree on the table and its radios.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-059, repo-frontend-p9-060 and trace-e2e-p9-020 show the same columns and radio labels today.

requirements.statement: The picker's Address column shows each address line on its own line, not joined by commas.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 prints one line per address line, which reads more easily in a narrow column.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Address column joins address lines, town, county and postcode with commas on one line (repo-frontend-p9-061, trace-e2e-p9-024).

requirements.statement: Each picker row ends with a 'View' link that opens that address in the INS address book, carrying a return path that brings the trader back to the same picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows an address's details on the address book's own page rather than in an expander; the address book belongs to the INS frontend, so its view page has to honour the return to the animals picker.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each row has a 'View details' disclosure that expands in place with the full record (repo-frontend-p9-062, repo-frontend-p9-063, trace-e2e-p9-026); the tests repo proves it expands without navigating (repo-tests-p5-014).

requirements.statement: Reopening a picker for a party that already has an address picked from the book pre-selects that address's radio; a copy that was edited, or whose record has gone from the book, opens with nothing selected.
requirements.why: The prototype pre-selects the current choice, and the real picker already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-073 and trace-animals-fit-p14-070 show the saved address pre-selected today.

requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on a picker with no address chosen shows no error: it returns to the roles and addresses page and leaves the party as it was, empty or holding its earlier address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader leave a picker without choosing; completeness is checked by the task status and the review, not by the picker.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving with nothing chosen keeps an address already held (repo-frontend-p9-079), but with none held it re-renders the picker with status 400 and 'Select a <party> from the list' (repo-frontend-p9-080, trace-animals-fit-p14-050 to -054).

requirements.statement: Saving a picker with an address that is not in the organisation's book, or has been deleted since the page loaded, saves nothing and re-renders the picker with status 400, an error summary 'There is a problem' and the party's error: 'Select a place of origin from the list', 'Select a consignor from the list', 'Select a consignee from the list', 'Select an importer from the list' or 'Select a place of destination from the list' (and their Welsh), the summary link going to the first address radio, or to the search box when there are no rows.
requirements.why: A real constraint the prototype cannot express: the notification must never hold a party copied from a record the organisation does not have, so today's refusal stays for that case.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-081 shows an id not in the organisation's book, or soft-deleted, refused with the party error today.

requirements.statement: Each of the five party pickers (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination) and the CPH number page end with a single primary 'Save and continue' button, with no 'Save and return to hub' button and no cancel link.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled this same difference (rule (b)): only pages the overview links to end with the three return controls, and a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone; the pickers are reached from the roles and addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-078, trace-e2e-p9-045 and trace-animals-fit-p15-030 show the pickers ending with 'Save and continue' alone today, and document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-057 records the CPH number page built the same way under DR1 rule (b). The permanent address page follows the same rule (req-748).

requirements.statement: Choosing an address on a picker and pressing 'Save and continue' saves on the notification a copy of that record (the record it came from, name, phone, email and address) and returns to the roles and addresses page, or to check your answers under change context. The roles and addresses page names each party from that copy, never from the address book, including after submission.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real service both save the chosen address against the party and return to the page; the copy keeps the notification stable when the book changes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-085, repo-frontend-p9-086 and trace-e2e-p9-044 show the copy saved and the redirect to the roles and addresses page today.

requirements.statement: If saving a picked address fails with a recoverable backend error, the picker re-renders with status 500, the recoverable-error message and the choice still selected.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the trader must not lose their choice when the save fails.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-088 shows this behaviour today.

requirements.statement: Each party picker offers only the organisation's addresses whose roles include that party's role: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters each picker to its role, so a trader is not offered a GB importer as a place of origin; DR1 found the unfiltered list a live defect on all the pickers, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles because DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all five pickers search one undifferentiated book with no address type (repo-frontend-p9-047), so every role offers the same addresses (trace-animals-fit-p14-045).

requirements.statement: The consignor picker offers addresses saved for the consignor role, including any saved as an exporter; there is no separate exporter party. How the address book records those roles is the address book's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's consignor section covers the exporter too, and accepts addresses saved as either. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 leaves the field shape of address roles to the address book service, so the prototype's type values are not copied.

requirements.statement: An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one saved address be reused across parties, such as the same company as consignee and importer.

requirements.statement: The address book (trade-imports-address-book) holds one or more roles on each address record and lets the animals frontend list an organisation's addresses for one role, unpaginated and still excluding deleted records; the animals frontend asks for the picker's role. The record's field shape for roles is the address book service's own design, not the prototype's.
requirements.why: DR1 found role filtering needs a typed address record, which no frontend can fake; the address book is one of this programme's repos, so the record shape and the role-aware list are built here. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles (inc-087) and leaves their field shape to the address book. Collecting the roles when an address is saved is the address-book and party-address-add-and-edit areas' work.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address-book record carries no type and its list call takes only a page and a search text (repo-frontend-p9-047, repo-frontend-p9-159).

requirements.statement: An address-book record that has no role yet (every record saved before roles exist) is offered on every party picker until it is given a role, in the compose stack and in CDP alike.
requirements.why: Records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and DR1's inc-048 judgement rules out filtering them on a guess, which would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants (c-101).

requirements.statement: In stub mode, each canned address-book record carries one or more roles, so the stub-mode pickers filter by role as the real ones do.
requirements.why: The stub mirrors the tests repo's address-book fixture record for record and is what local development and the frontend suite run against; without roles it cannot show role filtering.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the stub is 13 untyped records (repo-frontend-p9-168, repo-frontend-p9-169).

requirements.statement: Each party picker lists its addresses newest first, so an address just added through the address book appears at the top.
requirements.why: The prototype lists newly added addresses first, and the real picker already lists the book newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p5-017 and trace-e2e-p9-030 show newest-first listing today.

requirements.statement: When a search matches no address, the picker shows 'No addresses match your search.' in place of the table, and still offers 'Save and continue'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not show an empty result; the real picker's message tells the trader why the list is empty, and nothing in the prototype contradicts it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-064 and trace-animals-fit-p15-015 show the message today.

requirements.statement: Every address-book read from the animals frontend is made on the server, for the signed-in session's organisation only, carrying that organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the request tracing header; with no organisation in the session no read is made.
requirements.why: A real authorisation constraint: the address book trusts the organisation header, so the frontend's scoping is what keeps one organisation's addresses from another.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-155 to repo-frontend-p9-157 show this scoping today.

requirements.statement: A deleted address-book record is never offered on a picker; fetching one by id tells a deletion apart from a missing record, and any other failed address-book response is an error.
requirements.why: Deleted addresses must not be chosen again; the real service already relies on the address-book API for this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-160 and repo-frontend-p9-163 show deleted records kept off the picker today.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend reads the address book and never writes to it; adding a record goes through the INS frontend, and the animals journey serves no create-address page of its own.
requirements.why: The INS frontend is the address book's only writer; how Design Release 2.1's in-journey add page is met belongs to the party-address-add-and-edit area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-153 and repo-tests-p5-026 show the frontend reading only today.

requirements.statement: Every new or changed string on the roles and addresses page and the party pickers has a Welsh counterpart in the same change, still marked as a machine draft awaiting translator sign-off.
requirements.why: The real service is bilingual, and DR1 asked for each copy change in both languages; the prototype has no Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Welsh exists, as an unreviewed machine draft, only for the current strings (repo-frontend-p9-029, repo-frontend-p9-089).

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page and every party picker have no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 A and AA and 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: The real pages pass today and must keep passing as they change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-176, repo-frontend-p9-188 and trace-animals-fit-p14-020 show clean axe scans today.

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search is labelled 'Enter a country'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches the place of origin list by country, with this label; its specs assert the wording, and nothing overrides it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every picker, place of origin included, labels its search 'Search' (repo-frontend-p9-053).

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search has the hint 'Enter each country that the consignment will travel through'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives this hint on the place of origin search.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the place of origin search's hint is 'Name, address or country' (repo-frontend-p9-053).

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search box shows the placeholder 'Search for a country'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 prompts for a country inside the box.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search box has no placeholder (repo-frontend-p9-053).

requirements.statement: The place of origin picker's search is a country autocomplete: with JavaScript, it keeps the rows whose country contains the typed text, or exactly matches a country picked from the suggestions, and an empty box shows every row; without JavaScript, submitting a country narrows the list to that country on the server.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows the place of origin list by country; DR1 judged the server-side search must stay as the fallback without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the place of origin picker has the same free-text server search as every other picker (repo-frontend-p9-055).

requirements.statement: The prototype's fixed demonstration addresses (nine places of origin, nine consignors, six consignees and importers, three places of destination) are not built into the real service.
requirements.why: They are the prototype's seed data; the real pickers list the organisation's own address book.

requirements.statement: The prototype's page paths (/roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination under /design-release-2.1) replace the real service's routes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling sam-2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides URL paths and no increment changes an existing real path to match it; the real service keeps /addresses and its /select routes, in both the live-animals and the germinal-products sets.

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page's Change links drop the visually hidden party name, as the prototype's do.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the prototype's identical 'Change' links are an accessibility gap a sighted user cannot see, not a design choice; the real links keep naming the party for screen-reader users.

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set's roles and addresses page shows only the five party sections (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) for every germinal commodity: no CPH number section and no permanent address section, and the germinal set serves no CPH number or permanent address page behind them.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the CPH number out for 05111000 and 05119985 and walks germinal products through five address roles only. Ruling sam-2026-10-09 makes germinal products its own set, leaves the CPH number and permanent address pages out of it, and splits req-574 so this germinal half sits in the germinal set's increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no germinal-products set; germinal products run through the live-animals set, whose CPH row is the default and exempts only 0101 and 01061900 (trace-animals-fit-p14-027, repo-frontend-p9-019), so 05111000 and 05119985 are asked for a CPH number.

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set has its own roles and addresses page and its own five party pickers, copied from the live-animals set's addresses feature once this programme has built it, under the germinal set's own journey and routes with the live-animals slugs. Every roles-and-addresses and picker requirement in this area holds in the germinal copy too, apart from req-574 and req-575; the copy keeps the live-animal hints word for word, including 'The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain' and the place of destination's 'unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours'.
requirements.why: Ruling sam-2026-10-09 (option B) makes germinal products a sibling set in the animals frontend whose pages are copies of their live-animals feature folders plus the prototype's germinal differences, and calls that duplication accepted and desired. Design Release 2.1 shows germinal products the same roles page and wording as live animals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page and the five pickers exist only in the live-animals set (repo-frontend-p9-001, repo-frontend-p9-046).

requirements.statement: The roles and addresses page and the party pickers keep the real service's routes and form fields that the k6 performance scripts drive: the addresses page and the five /select pickers, the picker's search text field q submitted with action=search (also by the new search icon button), the address radio party saved with action=save, and a picker save landing back on the addresses page; a picker search still answers a 255-character search term.
requirements.why: Ruling sam-2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides URL paths or form field names, and that trade-imports-performance-tests joins only inc-129; keeping these names means no change here breaks the k6 journey, so performance tests need no row of their own for this area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-054, trace-animals-fit-p14-037 and trace-animals-fit-p14-061 show the q field, action=search, the party radio and action=save today, as repo-perftests-p1-049 drives them.

requirements.statement: The prototype's form field names on these pages replace the real service's: per-role radio names (placeOfOriginAddressId, consignorAddressId, consigneeAddressId, importerAddressId, placeOfDestinationAddressId), the action values continue, hub and same-as-<source>:<role>, and a search field named search.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling sam-2026-10-09 says the prototype never decides query parameter or form field names, and kept prototype content is built without its field shape. The real pickers keep party, q and their own action values; the same-as buttons are named in the real service's conventions.

conflicts.about: Whether the roles and addresses page becomes headed sections with insets, as the prototype draws it, or keeps its summary list.

positions.says: Each section is an h2 heading with its hint below and the chosen address in an inset.
DR1 judged that the requirement is that the address is visible, not that the component matches; a summary list may stay.
DR1 judged 'Not added yet' out of scope because it follows from the summary-list component choice.
The page lists the parties as summary-list rows.

conflicts.outcome: The DR1 judgement on this same difference wins over the prototype default, as sam-2026-10-07 directs: the summary list stays, with 'Not added yet' on empty rows, and every answered row shows the full address (req-571). The prototype's headed-section markup is set aside; its address content stands.

conflicts.about: Whether the fraud warning ends with a full stop.

positions.says: The warning reads 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud' with no full stop.
The warning reads 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud.'

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default; DR1 asked for the same change. The full stop goes.

conflicts.about: Whether each empty row's add link names what it adds or reads 'Add'.

positions.says: Each section's link names it: 'Add a place of origin', 'Add a consignor' and so on, and 'Add a CPH number'.
Every empty row's link reads 'Add', with the party in visually hidden text.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, and DR1 asked for the same six strings: each empty row gets its named link, and the now-redundant visually hidden text goes. Today's 'Change' link once a party is answered stands.

conflicts.about: Whether an answered party row shows the whole address or only the name.

positions.says: An answered section shows the name, each address line and the country on the last line.
An answered row shows the chosen address's name only.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, and DR1 asked for the same: every answered row shows the full address, inside the kept summary list (c-087).

conflicts.about: Which commodity codes leave out the CPH number section.

positions.says: Commodity codes 05111000 and 05119985 show only the five address sections, with no CPH number, as do 0101 and 01061900.
The CPH row shows by default and is withheld only for two exempt codes, horses (0101) being one.
The germinal set leaves out the CPH number page.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins on what germinal products are asked: no CPH number. Ruling sam-2026-10-09, ranked first, decides how: germinal products become their own set, which leaves out the CPH number page and section (req-consignment-parties-001), and the germinal lines leave the live-animals catalogue, so the live-animals set keeps exempting only 0101 and 01061900 (req-574) rather than adding the germinal codes to its exemption list.

conflicts.about: Where 'Save and continue' on the roles and addresses page goes.

positions.says: It goes to the contact address for consignment page, or to the overview when every overview section is complete.
It saves nothing and goes to the overview, or back to check your answers under change context.
The addresses page's Continue leads to the CPH number page.
A page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on Save and continue, and Roles and addresses opened from the overview no longer runs on to the CPH number page.

conflicts.outcome: Ruling sam-2026-10-09 ranks first for a page opened from its overview task: it returns to the overview (req-1615, c-204), with no ?from=hub marker, only the live flow's fallback changing. On a new notification's opening run the prototype wins by default: continue goes to the contact address page, not the CPH number page, or to the overview once every section is complete. Today's return to check your answers under change context stands, as the prototype draws no change context.

conflicts.about: Whether the picker's 'Add a new address' is a secondary button beside the heading or a plain link under the intro.

positions.says: A secondary 'Add a new address' button sits beside the heading.
'Add a new address' is a plain link inside a paragraph under the description, not a button.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default on how the control looks and where it sits; where it leads is the party-address-add-and-edit area's, and stub mode still leaves it out because there is no address service to add to.

conflicts.about: How a picker lists and searches its addresses: one page with a live filter, or five a page with a server search.

positions.says: DR1 judged the portable half to be one page, no pagination, count above the table, with the server-side search kept as the no-JavaScript fallback and a live filter on top.
The table filters in the browser as the user types, on name, address or country.
The picker shows five addresses a page.
The picker paginates with a 'Next' link and marks the current page.

conflicts.outcome: The DR1 judgement, which agrees with the prototype on one page and a live filter and adds the no-JavaScript fallback, wins over the prototype default and today's pagination: one page per role, live filter with JavaScript, the server search kept behind a submitting search button, and the 'Selected address' inset dropped. It lands with role filtering (req-608) so a page is the role's addresses, not the whole book.

conflicts.about: How the picker's results count is worded.

positions.says: The count reads 'Showing <visible> out of <total> results'.
The table caption reads 'Showing <shown> of <total> addresses'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, and DR1 asked for the same wording; the count moves out of the table caption to sit under the 'Select an address' heading.

conflicts.about: Whether the picker's Address column shows one line per address line or one comma-joined line.

positions.says: The Address column has one line per address line.
The Address column joins the address parts with commas.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: one line per address line.

conflicts.about: Whether a picker row shows an address's details through a 'View' link to the address book or a 'View details' expander.

positions.says: Each row has a 'View' link that opens the address in the address book with a return path to the picker.
Each row has a 'View details' disclosure.
View details expands in place, without navigating, so nothing typed or ticked is lost.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: each row gets a 'View' link to the INS address book with a return to the picker. Cross-service behaviour is a constraint the prototype cannot express, but it does not prevent this: the INS frontend is in the programme and must honour the return path. The tests repo's in-place expander test changes with it.

conflicts.about: What happens when a picker is saved with no address chosen.

positions.says: Submitting with no address chosen shows no error and returns to the roles and addresses page with the section unchanged.
A picker continued with nothing chosen returns to the roles page unchanged.
With nothing selected and no address held, the picker re-renders with status 400 and the party's error.
An id not in the organisation's book, or soft-deleted, is refused with the same party error.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default for a blank save: no error, back to the roles and addresses page, party unchanged. The ruling's validation override covers constraints the prototype cannot express, and a blank pick on a draft is not one: the prototype designs it explicitly and its specs assert it. Refusing a record that is not, or is no longer, in the organisation's book is such a constraint, so that refusal and its party errors stay (req-604).

conflicts.about: Whether a party picker ends with 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub' as well as 'Save and continue'.

positions.says: Under DR1 rule (b) the party pickers adopt the save-actions macro passing false, so they end with the primary button alone.
A select page's buttons are 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to hub', with a 'Cancel and return to hub' link.
Each picker has 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
Each role picker has two buttons, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to hub'.
'Save and return to hub' on a select page saves and goes to the overview.
Save and return to hub on a role picker goes to the overview.
Save and return to hub on a picker saves and goes to the overview.
While amending, a select page shows 'Save and return', 'Save and continue' and a 'Save and return to overview' button.

conflicts.outcome: DR1 already judged this same difference (rule (b), built as ruled): pages reached from another page end with the primary button alone, and the party pickers are reached from the roles and addresses page. The DR1 judgement overrides the prototype, so the pickers keep 'Save and continue' alone, and the prototype's 'hub' versus 'overview' wording on the pickers falls away with the buttons.

conflicts.about: Whether DR1's blocks on the address pages (the address-space collision block and the typed-record block) keep these differences from being built.

positions.says: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
Every increment that changes an address-selection page is blocked until the team's address work settles.
The consignment party page increments are blocked for the same reason.
A later ruling blocks all six journey pickers.
inc-056, inc-052, inc-045 and inc-063 were blocked because they touch live address work on the party page.
inc-048, role filtering of the pickers, is blocked as needs-backend.
inc-065, the list heading and count, is blocked by the address-space ruling.
inc-055, one page narrowed as you type, is blocked by the address-space ruling.

conflicts.outcome: The sam-2026-10-07 ruling ranks first. DR1's blocks defer work for collision or dependency reasons and record no judgement on the differences themselves (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-054), so they do not override the prototype. The typed address record they waited on is built in this programme, which includes trade-imports-address-book. DR1's judgements inside those rows (the address must be visible; keep the server search as the no-JavaScript fallback) still apply.

conflicts.about: What the role-filtered pickers offer for address-book records saved before addresses carried roles.

positions.says: A picker lists only addresses whose types include the section's role.
Filtering on a guess would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants.

conflicts.outcome: Each party picker filters typed address-book records by its role, as Design Release 2.1 does (prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063); an existing record with no role yet is offered on every party picker until it is given one, in the compose stack and in CDP alike, because DR1's inc-048 judgement (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-051) rules out hiding addresses the trader legitimately wants on a guess, and records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express. The stub-mode records are each given roles so stub mode shows the filtering.

conflicts.about: Whether the place of origin picker searches by country with transit-country wording or uses the free-text search the other pickers use.

positions.says: The place of origin picker searches by country: label 'Enter a country', hint 'Enter each country that the consignment will travel through', placeholder 'Search for a country'.
Every picker's search is labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default. The hint reads like transit-country copy (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-127), but the prototype's specs assert it (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p3-035) and no DR1 judgement or real constraint overrides it, so the label, hint, placeholder and country filter are adopted as drawn.

conflicts.about: Whether the consignor party is named 'Consignor' or 'Consignor or exporter'.

positions.says: The consignor section is headed 'Consignor', covering the exporter too.
The consignor party is titled 'Consignor or exporter'.
The hub's party roles include 'Consignor or exporter'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default, and DR1 asked for the same rename: 'Consignor' on the row, picker heading, page title and hidden link text, English and Welsh, with the id, route and address-book role unchanged. The overview task hint 'Consignor or Exporter, ...' stays, as the prototype keeps it too.

conflicts.about: What makes the 'Roles and addresses' task complete.

positions.says: The task is complete only when every section shown for the consignment is complete.
The task shows Complete once all five parties are picked and the page is submitted.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: every shown section, the CPH number or permanent address included, must be complete.

conflicts.about: How the picker's search label and button look.

positions.says: The search label is medium-heading styled and the search runs from an icon button with aria-label 'Search'.
The search label is small and a secondary 'Search' text button sits next to the field.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default on appearance: a medium label and an icon button named 'Search'. The button submits the form, per DR1's no-JavaScript judgement (c-094).
